question: What does `verify` of an AC-3 family stream want the samples of the stream for, and what is reading the stream without them worth?
method: What the reports of the family have of the samples was read from the code and counted over the streams of the family in the corpus. A decoder was given a way of making no samples, and the commands that read a stream and do not listen to it were put onto it. What that is worth was measured inside one binary, as `verify` against `verify --decode`, which are the stream read without its samples and with them: turn and turn about, nine runs each, bound to the fast cores. The binary of the change was measured against the binary of main the same way for `info`, `verify`, `emdf` and `oamd`, and with `tools/bench.py --compare`, five runs, for every command of the comparison. That comparison first called a delivery to PCM slower, and what that was is followed here through the builds that told it apart. That no report and no delivery changed was looked for over the corpus (`tools/old_new.py --decode-all`) and in the campaign of evidence 22. The streams are media and are not in the repository.

what_a_report_has_of_the_samples.the_figure: the level of the core under each clip gain of the JOC payloads (`JOC core level:`), which `verify` and `info` print for a stream whose payloads carry more than one clip gain; nothing else a command of this family reports, and nothing its verdict rests on, is of the samples

the_change_inside_one_binary.how: `verify` over `verify --decode` of the binary of the change, medians of nine runs, bound to the fast cores
the_change_inside_one_binary.reading: a stream that has the row is read without its samples up to the frame where a second clip gain shows, and then again from its first frame with them: the frames before that one are paid for twice. The figure is of every frame from the first, so there is no reading it cheaper without knowing beforehand that the stream has it

which_part_of_the_change.reading: the decoder of the change does not slow a delivery; the binary with the commands of the change does, and the commands changed nothing a delivery runs but the pass around the loop that writes its bytes, which keeps two counters more

the_loop_that_writes_the_bytes.how: that loop pushed the samples of a frame onto a new vector, a sample of every channel at a time. Written a channel at a time into a buffer of the size of the frame, in main and in the change, four binaries turn and turn about
the_loop_that_writes_the_bytes.reading: the two builds that were a tenth apart are within some hundredths of each other, and both are faster than main: what was slower was what the compiler had made of that loop in one build and not in the other

result.what_is_not_covered: Every stream of the family in the corpus, and the fixture, has six blocks a frame. That a frame nobody listens to is counted as the samples its blocks would have made is tested on the buffer by itself, for frames of one, two, three and six blocks, and the decoder that listens asserts in a debug build that the count is the one the transform made; no test puts a stream of shorter frames through both decoders. A stream that has the level of the core in its report is read twice up to its second clip gain: two streams of the corpus, which take 110.3 and 123.9 per cent of the time.

reading: Of the 76 streams of the family in the corpus, 2 have a figure of the samples in their report. `verify` of the others reads every frame to its last bit and makes no samples, in 45.8 to 59.4 per cent of the time it takes with them, inside one binary, on eight streams; `info`, `emdf` and `oamd` with it, 45.7 to 58.1 per cent of what they took on main. The two that have the figure are read twice up to their second clip gain and take 110.3 and 123.9 per cent. A delivery to PCM, which the first comparison had 3.5 to 12.2 per cent slower, was slower by what the compiler made of the loop that writes its bytes; written a channel at a time it takes 96.4 and 96.8 per cent of the time it took on main. No report and no delivery changes over the corpus.
